Class ReportsView

java.lang.Object
com.squad83.views.ReportsView
public class ReportsView extends Object
Provides the JavaFX manager interface for creating and viewing operational reports from the Squad 83 point-of-sale PostgreSQL database.

Managers select a report from a drop-down menu, optionally choose a date range, and view query results in a table whose columns are generated from the result-set metadata. The available reports are:

  • Sales by Item: quantities sold and sales totals for each menu item over a selected date range, including only completed orders.
  • Daily Sales: number of completed orders and total sales by day.
  • Best Selling Items: menu items ranked by quantities sold.
  • Employee Sales: completed order counts and sales by employee.
  • Peak Sales Hours: completed order counts and sales grouped by hour.
  • Sales by Payment Method: completed orders and sales by payment type.
  • Inventory Reorder: inventory items at or below their reorder levels.
  • Product Usage Chart: estimated ingredient usage for completed, top-level order items within a selected date range.
  • X-Report: hourly order and sales totals for the latest qualifying day, with an overall total, using XReportQuery.getSql().
  • Audit Report: counts and monetary totals for completed sales, voids, refunds, and discards within a selected date range.

This class uses static controls and helper methods to manage the report selection, query execution, display, and error dialogs.

  • Method Details

    • getView

      public static javafx.scene.Parent getView()
      Creates the manager reporting view and initializes its JavaFX controls.

      The view includes a report selector, start and end date pickers, buttons for generating and clearing a report, a results table, and a status label. Date pickers begin with a 30-day range and are enabled only for reports that support date filtering.

      Returns:
      the root Parent containing the reporting interface

    • usesTimeWindow

      private static boolean usesTimeWindow(String report)
      Determines whether a selected report accepts a start and end date.

      Only Sales by Item, Product Usage Chart, and Audit Report use the date pickers. Other reports use their own SQL-defined time scope.

      Parameters:
      report - the selected report name; may be null
      Returns:
      true when the report accepts a custom date range; false otherwise

    • generateReport

      private static void generateReport()
      Builds the SQL statement for the selected report and requests its results.

      The report selector determines which SQL query to use. Queries for completed-order reports filter by order status. For Sales by Item, Product Usage Chart, and Audit Report, a valid time window is required; loadReport(String, String) supplies its timestamp parameters. The X-Report SQL is supplied by XReportQuery.getSql().

      If no report is selected, the date range is invalid, or the selected report is unrecognized, an error dialog is displayed instead.

      The Audit Report groups the four supported transaction statuses (completed, voided, refunded, and discard) and uses a left join so categories with no matching orders still appear with zero totals.

    • validateDates

      private static boolean validateDates()
      Validates the start and end dates chosen for a time-window report.

      Both dates must be selected, and the start date must not be after the end date. Any invalid selection displays an explanatory dialog.

      Returns:
      true when both dates are present and ordered correctly; false otherwise

    • loadReport

      private static void loadReport(String sql, String reportName)
      Executes the selected report query and presents its rows in the table.

      A JDBC PreparedStatement binds date parameters when required, using an inclusive start timestamp and an exclusive timestamp at the beginning of the day after the selected end date. The method uses ResultSetMetaData to create table columns dynamically, converts returned values to strings, and updates the result count/status label. SQL errors are displayed through showError(String, String).

      Parameters:
      sql - the SQL query for the selected management report
      reportName - the report title used to determine date binding and describe the displayed results

    • clearReport

      private static void clearReport()
      Resets the reporting screen to its initial state.

      Clears the selected report and results, restores the default 30-day date range, and replaces the status message with the initial prompt.

    • showError

      private static void showError(String title, String message)
      Displays a modal JavaFX error dialog with the supplied message.
      Parameters:
      title - the title displayed in the error dialog window
      message - the explanation shown to the manager
